messages.subject: Exclusions
parts:
I am setting up transects right now to do some line distance sampling for an endangered fly and there are quite a few shrubs the transects go through. Some of the shrubs are centered on the transects and it is clear the whole shrub is considered an exclusion, however, sometimes the shrub is only blocking the transect by a foot or so. My question is how far off the transect does the observer have to step in order for the shrub to be considered an exclusion? Thanks.

Tara Graham

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Exclusions
parts:
Tara

I think you intend not to sample parts of your study area that are "shrubs".  I would propose that instead you place your transects through the shrubs, but the observers walk around (rather than through) the shrubs.  However, to use conventional distance sampling, you must still ensure that flies on the transect line can be detected with certainty.

You need not be standing upon the transect to detect objects on the transect.  An example of this survey technique applied to desert tortoises is shown here

Observers may need to stop walking and gaze at the portion of the transect passing through the shrub to ensure detectability is certain.
